central_ecological_question: Does an independently sampled seven-island 42-trap SLAM native/mixed/exotic forest network support a forest-habitat community filtering test with balanced island and repeated temporal sampling, capable of evaluating whether native and introduced arthropod assemblages respond differently to forest vegetation context? Primary evidence would be SAME-method source site matched, not BALA or PRIBES raw reuse.
intended_new_target: Among within-island SLAM forest plot pairs, is introduced beetle compositional similarity systematically greater across contrasting forest vegetation habitats than endemic/native beetle similarity? Does mixed vegetation resemble native forests in endemic assemblages or exotic forests in introduced assemblages under comparable sampling periods?

source.author_published_caution: Borges & Lhoumeau source paper described 2012–2021 samples, SLAM trap sites mostly preserved wet forests, some mixed with exotic trees. One former resource text reported 14924 instead of official v1.7 14922 Occurrence rows; use original exact archive checks rather than assumption.

limitations: SLAM traps are flight/crawl interception, BALA native-forest Pitfall and PRIBES ruderal vegetation-beating are distinct detection channels.
Forest vegetation composition may be observationally confounded with altitude, forest age, island climate, management and isolation.
The published SLAM original can overlap previous SLAM/PRIBES forest sites; absence of proven disjoint site identifiers prevents a formal replication claim.
Source paper's 2022 endemic/native/exotic records and habitat associations are already prior art, not newly discovered facts.
Single Azores archipelago; no direct habitat-to-forest species colonization, extinction or source-sink rescue observations.
